To sustain participation and expand grid beneficial flexibility, the team was going to investigate pairing kWh- oriented incentives with ongoing annual kW-based incentives modeled on the Wattsmart Program. Enabling measures included controllable HVAC through connected smart thermostats, and CT 2045 enabled water heaters, federated on the PNNL VOLTTRON platform. In multifamily settings, tenants with residential accounts that do not include time of use or demand charges were going to be able to enroll devices for annual participation incentives, while owners with commercial common area accounts that include demand charges were to realize direct bill reductions alongside kW-based incentives. Together, these program designs were going to establish incentive levels for adoption and retention at individual sites, satisfying Milestone 9.2.1. 30 6.1.10 Task 10: Deploy Cybersecurity Plan and Framework The project team focused on improving the Cybersecurity Plan based on multiple iterations with PNNL and BHE IT’s cybersecurity office. The Cybersecurity Plan has been evaluated by PNNL against the Phase A and Phase B checklists, and after different versions and improvements, it has successfully completed both checklists. The Cybersecurity Plan integrates a detailed data flow and system description of all the different facilities and energy assets, a description of preventive cybersecurity mechanisms based on the NIST Cybersecurity Framework, and a table that maps vulnerabilities and risks with the defined solutions. The Cybersecurity Plan was planned to be a live document that was to be regularly updated along with the project progress to integrate any changes in the data flow and additional vulnerabilities and risks, as well as novel defense mechanisms that are constantly being created by the cybersecurity community. 6.1.10.1 Subtask 10.1.0: Develop threat detection and response solutions The first layer of defense against cyber threats consisted of identifying the main threats and risks specific for the system architecture and then following best practices to prevent malicious actors from impacting the system or mitigate their impact if they are successful. The Cybersecurity Plan underwent multiple iterations and updates with valuable feedback from BHE IT’s cybersecurity office and Pacific Northwest National Lab (PNNL). The plan had already been evaluated and approved against the Phase A and Phase B checklists by the PNNL cybersecurity team, and it included significant improvements from the version submitted during BP1, such as a table with role- based access details for each location and the Vulnerability, Threat, Risk, and a Mitigation Table that summarized the identified vulnerabilities with their respective threats, the mitigation strategy associated to each vulnerability, and the status of such strategy. The status of the mitigation strategies corresponds to: • Implemented – threat is mitigated due to implementation of the mitigation within the system • In Progress – the mitigation strategy is in the process of being implemented but it is still not completed • Transferred – the threat risk has been transferred to a different entity and is out of scope • Accepted – the threat risk is accepted,
